recipes.name: Beef Shish Kebabs for Freezer Cooking
ingredients_raw: 1 red bell pepper, cut into 1 inch pieces
1.5 pounds beef sirloin, cut into 1 inch cubes

steps.text: Place zucchini, bell pepper, and pineapple in a large bowl. Drizzle with oil; toss to coat. Portion mixture among plastic resealable freezer bags.

Whisk ketchup, water, steak sauce, sugar, vinegar, and Worcestershire sauce together in a separate bowl. Add beef cubes; toss to coat. Divide beef mixture among bags, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bags; freeze.
Thaw desired portion(s) in refrigerator before cooking, 8 hours to overnight. Meanwhile, soak skewers in warm water, 30 minutes to overnight.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.
Remove beef, vegetables, and pineapple from marinade and shake off excess. Discard marinade. Alternate beef, vegetables, and pineapple onto skewers.
Cook on the preheated grill, flipping occasionally, until cooked to your liking, about 10 minutes total for medium-rare.

raw_recipe.headline: Beef Shish Kebabs for Freezer Cooking
raw_recipe.description: This beef shish kebabs for freezer cooking recipe uses pre-portioned beef and veggies. All you do is thaw, assemble, and grill for an easy dinner.

review.reviewBody: I made this dish six times for each member of my dinner exchange club. All six said their families loved this. My husband does too. Very easy and do not feel any changes are needed. I bought meat already cut for kabobs to save time.

I love this recipe and get requests to make this often. I marinate the meat overnight but use fresh veggies as the frozen veggies are soft. I separate some of the marinade before adding it all to the meat so I can baste the skewers as they are grilling. Been using this recipe for several years. :)

Mmmm, these were SO GOOD! I loved how the beef was juicy, but not oily or herby like other kabob recipes. Instead of freezing them, I just put the vegetables and meat in 2 separate small ziplock bags and refridgerated them 4-5 hours before cooking. The only changes I made was for the meat I had 2 NY Strip steaks. I trimmed the fat and cut them into 1" cubes. Out of everything I got 8 kabobs and at most about 3 servings. I did 1/2 red and 1/2 green bell pepper for the peppers, as it was what I had, and I also subbed white wine vinegar for the cider vinegar for the same reason. I definitely plan to make this again, but next time I will double it!

This is delicious! The sauce is positively yummy! I left the beef cubes in the sauce for over 24 hours so the flavor was really prominent. I did not freeze anything but did cut the veggies and fruit the day before. I also added Asian pear to the skewers and sliced onion. I highly suggest saving some of this sauce as a "dip" for additional meat. Maybe try this on burgers? Good stuff!

I bought top sirloin and never froze it. Marinated it per instructions for about 4.5 hours. 
Same with the shrimp except only marinated it about 1 hour. 
The steak was very tender however the marinade was overwhelming. The taste of soy sauce overpowered it as well as the oil. 
The shrimp marinade also was mostly the flavor of the olive oil. I don't know, maybe I shouldn't have marinated them for the amount of time I did??
I also used yellow and purple onions, squash as well as red and orange bell peppers.

It was excellent the marinade was so good my wife said they were the best shish kebabs she ever had and didn’t even need ketchup. I made the brown rice recipe from this site the share of the shish kebabs on top of it.
I added things to the shish kebab taters tomatoes onions Mushrooms.

good idea for the beef,but i waited till ready to make for veggies
because they get soggy when thawed from frozen and it only takes a short time to cut them up fresh

I made these fresh (didn't bother to freeze any) and they were SO delicious. I didn't change a thing (except added a few white onion slices). We really enjoyed the flavor combinations from the pineapple, meat, and veggies. My husband asked if we could eat these every Wednesday, so I might have to try freezing some for next time.
A big hit! Used no zucchini (Not on hand) but more green and red and orange peppers. Didn't freeze but made it for 2 days in a row. Really love it!
Added some onion to the skewer. Became a family favorite the first time we made it!
Loved the marinade so much that I made it again tonight, omitted the water, and basted pork chops with it. Fabulous!!
marinade was so so, Vegetables were good raw and unfrozen ist night. After freezing they were just a mushy soft mess. I will not use this method again.

We loved this recipe! So easy to just pull out of the freezer for a busy day! Healthy and flavorful. I do like to make the beef in the marinade and freeze, and then use fresh vegetables with the defrosted beef.
the best kebab i've ever made.... my husband loves the recipe
